newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa to handle Thai, United, SAS carg.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa to handle Thai, United, SAS carg.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo is taking over air cargo handling for three partner airlines at Frankfurt airport, the partner airlines said.
Thai Airways International, United Airlines and SAS Cargo said they were moving into a new freight centre beside the Lufthansa Cargo Centre.

The airlines were previously handled by Frankfurt airport owner and operator Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG). At various stages over the past three years the three have signed cargo partnership deals with Lufthansa.
Thai and United told freight forwarders in a letter they moved into the new Lufthansa freight hall on April 28.
Lufthansa would be responsible for documentation and physical handling of both export and import shipments for the two airlines, it said.
Thai's Germany cargo manager, Guillermo Valencia, told Reuters: "Lufthansa will do the handling with staff dedicated for the alliance partners."
"This is a step forward in the partnership between Thai and Lufthansa. We are developing it step by step," he added.
Freight forwarders would have improved delivery times and late acceptances since only three airlines were handled in the freight centre, he pointed out.
In a separate notice to forwarders, SAS Cargo said Lufthansa would take over physical handling for its flown export air freight.
But air cargo for long-haul destinations would continue to be trucked from the airline's Kelsterbach facilities to Scandinavia, it added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
